definition: A concentrated seasoning base spooned into the bowl before broth is added -- the actual salt and umami engine of the bowl, not a garnish.
Fermented, seasoned bamboo shoots with a distinctive savory tang and crunch -- a classic shoyu-ramen topping.
A soft-boiled egg marinated in a soy-based liquid until the yolk turns a deep, jammy amber.
Braised or roasted pork, most often belly or shoulder, sliced thin -- ramen's most common protein topping.
A noodle-only refill ordered into your existing bowl of broth, most associated with Hakata-style tonkotsu shops.
Alkaline mineral water added to ramen noodle dough, giving the noodles their characteristic spring, chew, and pale yellow tint.
Fat or oil -- most often referring to the aroma oil floated on the broth's surface just before serving.
A sheet of dried seaweed, typically propped against the bowl's edge -- meant to be dipped bite by bite rather than left to soak and go soft.
Scallion, or green onion -- a near-universal fresh, sharp garnish scattered over almost any bowl.
Toasted or lightly burnt black garlic oil -- the defining aroma oil of Kumamoto-style tonkotsu ramen.
